motivation: In clean Case A, the completed reduced space-time hybrid polynomial fit has reaction error about 0.188, exceeding its direct space-time weak reference. The reduced space hybrid also has residual error. A fixed derivative regularization weight may compete differently with differently scaled weak residuals. The earlier difference must not be interpreted as an intrinsic limitation of the space-time weak formulation.
hypothesis: Within the unchanged seven-coefficient family and saved residual matrices, changing only derivative regularization may materially alter the residual clean-case closure error. This control tests sensitivity to regularization relative to the implemented residual scales, not a universal normalization or an optimal tuning rule.
freeze_rule: Write this protocol and FREEZE.json with source, input and bundle hashes before running any conditions. Reject identity changes rather than updating a running study.
inputs: The same twenty hashed case_a/case_exp, clean/noise3, seeds 0..4 NPZ inputs used by reviewer-objective-controls-2026-10-15. Reuse saved per-term augmented QR matrices from its shared bundles; never regenerate fields or residual matrices.
family: D degree 2 and R degree 3, physical-state monomials, seven coefficients, unchanged from the completed objective controls.
solver: Import the frozen objective_controls.py float64 QR/SVD and positive_diffusion solver. No new ridge, normalization or optimizer tuning. Preserve full rank/stationarity/KKT logs and exact continuous quadratic diffusion minimum. Positive floor 1e-4, guard 1e-10.
reference_repetitions: Factor one has 80 existing conditions. Recompute using saved QR only, compare coefficients, losses and E_D/E_R with the original records, and explicitly mark repeated_reference. These do not constitute independent replications or new data. The remaining 240 conditions are new weight interventions.
reference_identity_tolerance: absolute plus relative difference <= 1e-10 * max(1, abs(reference)) for coefficients, each loss and E_D/E_R; discrepancies are failures, never silently replaced.
evaluation: Reuse the original uniform 256-state relative E_D/E_R metrics and observed enclosure checks; true closures only enter post-fit evaluation. Save all six raw and weighted losses, actual minimized objective, no-reg reduced objective, same-variant factor-one objective, and the same original space-weak full-hybrid objective for every fitted coefficient vector. This last common score uses original weights and space-weak matrices even for the space-time fits.
statistics: Show every case, noise setting, variant, factor and constraint. Mean and sample SD across five paired data seeds. Save seed-matched contrasts against factor one for each factor, with sample SD and descriptive t intervals. No selection of the best factor, seed, case or metric. Repeated conditions do not increase n.
mechanism_diagnostics: Report the weighted regularizer fraction of each fitted objective and changes in weak and no-reg residual losses. These are descriptive scales, not causal shares of closure error. Opposing movement of observation loss and regularization is interpreted within this fixed quadratic objective only.
presentation: One mechanism figure with A/Exp by clean/noise3, both reduced variants, both constraints, and E_D/E_R mean plus sample SD across the four factors; all full-precision condition data retained. Summary explicitly reports adverse, negligible and favorable changes without extending the factor grid.
failure_policy: Write per-condition status, exception or failed certificate and preserve original records. Incomplete groups are marked; the report never labels a failed condition successful. No protocol-changing retry.
limits: Exploratory control motivated by earlier results, not an independent preregistered confirmation. Five seeds; polynomial family differs from the neural family. No neural training, convergence claim, universal weak-form ranking, or truth-based hyperparameter selection. Reducing regularization still leaves rollout and anchor terms, so it does not reproduce the direct weak-only baseline.
